---
title: "Q-Learning"
description: "A model-free reinforcement-learning algorithm that learns action values using temporal-difference updates."
term: "Q-Learning"
letter: "Q"
category: "Reinforcement Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Q-learning teaches an agent which actions are valuable in different
situations. It can learn from rewards and experience without being given a
complete model of how the environment works.

## Technical explanation

Q-learning estimates the action-value function $Q(s,a)$, the expected
discounted return from taking action $a$ in state $s$ and then following an
optimal policy. A tabular update is
$Q(s,a)\leftarrow Q(s,a)+\alpha[r+\gamma\max_{a'}Q(s',a')-Q(s,a)]$.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

The algorithm is a foundational example of off-policy temporal-difference
learning. Its tabular form is simple, while extensions with function
approximation require care because training can be unstable and large
state-action spaces cannot be stored in a table.

## How it works

The agent explores by selecting actions, observes reward and next state, and
updates the value estimate toward the reward plus discounted best estimated
future value. A behavior policy may explore, while the target in the update
uses the greedy next action.

## Practical example

In a small grid-world, the agent can store one Q-value per state-action pair.
After each move it updates that value from the reward and the best value
estimated for the next state, gradually favoring paths with higher return.

## Common misconceptions

- Q-learning's learned Q-values are estimates; they are not guaranteed to
  be accurate from limited experience.
- The tabular algorithm does not scale directly to every large or
  continuous state space.
